findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed multiple temperature control for food safety (TCS) foods above 41F.
1) FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed raw shelled eggs sitting at an ambient temperature of 58F.
2) TCS foods in the kitchen prep cooler (including but not limited to raw hamburger, cut tomatoes, shredded lettuce, and cheese) to have internal temperatures between 56-59F.
The PIC verified the eggs and items in the prep cooler had been out since 8 AM (2 hours).  CORRECTED- items were moved under TIME AS CONTROL- to be used or discarded with a total of 4 hours (by 2PM). When items are unable to maintain temperature control (below 41F or above 135F) they must be used or discarded within 4 hours. Ensure all  temperature control for food safety (TCS) foods are held at or below 41F, OR marked to be used or discarded within 4 hours after removing from temperature control to limit the growth of pathogens.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

findings.title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
findings.comment:
Multiple incidents of bare hand contact were observed during today’s inspection:
1) The salad tongs at the server station were in contact with the food.
2) The ice scoop was in contact with the ice in the ice machine.
3) A bowl was stored as a scoop in tomato sauce in the walk in cooler. 
CORRECTED- the tongs and ice scoop were moved so that the handle was no longer in contact with the ready to eat (RTE) foods. The bowl was removed from the tomato sauce. Ensure scoops (that have handles) and tongs are stored in such a manner to prevent bare hand contamination. Improper hygiene practices are one of the top five risk factors for food borne illness.
findings.citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT. [P]

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Inspector observed ground beef (minimal internal temperature of 155F) stored above whole cuts of beef (minimal internal temperature of 145F). CORRECTED- the ground beef was moved below the whole cuts and education regarding surface area contaminants for ground products was provided. Inspector provided the PIC with a storage order handout. Ensure all animal proteins are stored by increasing internal cooking temperatures to prevent contamination of foods with lower (-no) cooking temperatures.

(A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the sanitizer bucket near the kitchen entry to have soap, and no measurable concentration of chemical sanitizer. CORRECTED- the sanitizer bucket (Chlorine bleach) was remade to 100 ppm. Ensure sanitizer buckets are made at a frequency to hold the sanitizing concentration of food contact surfaces as recommended by the manufacturer's label (50-200 ppm for Chlorine bleach). Do not use soap for chemical sanitation, as the soap and sanitizer combined decrease each product’s intended use.

A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A). findings.comment:
THIS IS A THREE TIMES REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed the following stored in the incorrect storage order: 

(1) The raw beef stored over various ready-to-eat foods in the double cooler to the left of the cookline (near the dish machine). During the inspection the raw beef was moved onto a bottom shelf. 

(2) Multiple containers of raw chicken stored over raw beef in the walk-in cooler. During the inspection the raw chicken was moved onto a bottom shelf. The facility stores all raw meat in the back left corner of the walk-in cooler and the inspector suggests labeling the bottom shelf for chicken storage only. 

Ensure that raw foods are stored below ready-to eat-foods and raw meats are stored according to internal cooking temperatures. Due to the amount of repeat violations the health educator will be reaching out to schedule food storage education at the facility.

findings.title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records.
findings.comment: Observed the prep cooler on the cookline is currently not functioning. The PIC was aware that the cooler was not functioning and prior to the inspection implemented a time-as-control (TAC) policy for temperature control for safety foods inside the cooler (cut tomatoes, lettuce, mayo, and cheese). The majority of the foods had already been removed from the cooler and only condiments and cut vegetables were being stored in the top. While they had implemented a TAC policy they were not writing down the time when food must be discarded. The PIC was aware of the time the foods were put into the cooler and during the inspection a note pad was brought to the prep table and the foods in temperature control were recorded. The PIC stated that a new part has already been ordered to fix the cooler, but until it is serviced they will continue to use TAC. The inspector will follow-up on 7/10/2025 to check on either the TAC procedure or that the cooler is properly functioning. Ensure that foods are properly marked to indicate the four hour TAC window until the cooler is cold holding foods at 41F or below.

findings.comment:

Person-in-charge immediately took corrective action with staff instructing them to never use the hand sink for any other purposes. Corrected on site. No follow-up required. findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
findings.comment:
During the inspection, inspector observed a can which was dented sharply along the upper seam in the rolling can storage rack. Inspector discussed the need check cans prior to accepting delivery to prevent costs associated with disposing of cans and ensure consumer safety by preventing the use of compromised cans. Cans dented along the seam where the integrity of the can is in question can be a source of botulism. The dented can observed by the inspector was immediately tossed. During a quick look of the remainder of the cans no dented cans were immediately apparent. Ensure that all cans are checked and that cans dented along any seem are not allowed into the rotation. A follow-up is being issued for 10-days (11/21/2022). Go through all cans in the facility to ensure that none are dented along a seam.

findings.comment: REPEAT #2: No CFM can provide evidence of allergen training. Ensure CFM in charge has allergen training certificate. Reference PA 100-0367.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment: Observed raw meat above RTE foods in R-I Cooler in kitchen area. Observed raw meat above raw vegetables. Corrected. Education provided. Raw meats have been moved below RTE foods and raw vegetables. Reference 3-302.11.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment: Observed knives in knife rack as well as knife near prep cooler to be soiled with debris. Ensure equipment is clean to sight and touch. Clean equipment. Corrected. Equipment will be cleaned. Reference 4-601.11(A).

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment: Observed several foods without date marking in the R-I Cooler near stove in kitchen. This included refried beans and noodles. Food shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a food establishment and if the food is held for more than 24 hours. Corrected. Employee will date mark products appropriately. All have been opened or made within 7 days. Reference 3-501.17.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment: REPEAT #1: Observed foods throughout facility to be exposed to environment. Ensure all foods are covered during storage to prevent contamination. Reference 3-307.11.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment: Observed dripper well to have significant amount of soil accumulation not being removed from well. Ensure running water removes all solids. Reference 3-304.12.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
REPEAT #1: Observed stoves to have soil accumulation. Ensure grills and stoves are cleaned as needed to prevent accumulation. Clean stoves. Reference 4-601.11(B) and (C).
Observed ice machine to have black residue present. Ensure ice machine is cleaned as needed. Reference 4-602.13.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment: Observed floor to be severly soiled near hood vent area. Clean flooring to prevent further accumulation. PIC stated floors are cleaned daily. Reference 6-501.12 (A & B).

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment: REPEAT #1: No CFM has allergen training. Ensure all CFMs have  certified allergen training. Obtain certificate. Reference PA 100-0367.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment: Observed employee wash hands and turn off faucet with hands. Ensure barrier is used to turn off water. Corrected. Education provided.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12  (P) Food employee improperly washed hands. Food employees shall properly wash their hands and exposed portion of their arms for at least 20 seconds, with approved soap and drying methods, according to this section of the food code. Reference 2-301.12.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment: Observed food debris in handwashing sink. Observed employee filling bucket up with handwashing sink. Handwashing sinks must be used for handwashing only. Corrected. Education provided.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11  (Pf) Hand washing sink must be used for handwashing only. Reference 5-205.11.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment: Observed several items to have no protective cover. Ensure all food is covered during storage. Ensure all food is protected against contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-307.11  (C) Food is not protected from contamination at multiple areas. Food shall be protected from contamination. Reference 3-307.11.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment: Observed forks, spoons, and knifes in disorganization. Ensure all utensils are laid in similiar manner to prevent contamination.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(A) and (C)  (C) Single-Use Articles are stored incorrectly near front. Single-Use Articles shall be stored: 1) in a clean and dry location; 2) away or protected from contamination; 3) at least six inches above the floor; 4) covered or inverted. Reference 4-903.11(A) and (C).

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: Observed large soilage on stove and ice machine. Clean non-food contact surfaces as needed.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13  (C) Soil residue present on Stove top. Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
No CFMs have food allergen training. Ensure all CFMS have food allergen training.
PA 100-0367. All certified food protection managers (CFPMs) working in a restaurant must complete additional allergen training using an approved allergen awareness training program.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment:
Observed handle of ice scooper down in ice.
Ice handle should be faced up away from ice to prevent contamination.
750-280 Food dispensing utensils shall be stored in the food with the handle extending out of the food; or stored clean and dry; or stored in running potable water dipper wells.

findings.title: Proper hygienic practices, eating/drinking/smoking (evidence)
findings.comment:
1) Observed personal drinks open near food.
2) Observed employees wiping hands on apron.
Hygenic practices should be used to prevent cross-contamination
750-510a Employees shall properly wash their hands any time their hands may have become contaminated and prior to handling food or clean equipment.

findings.title: Dishwashing facilities designed, constructed, operated (1. wash 2. rinse 3. sanitize)
findings.comment:
Observed mold around dishwasher area.
Dishwasher area must be free from mold and other debris.
750-830a Dish machines shall be properly installed and maintained in good repair. Dish machines shall be operated in accordance with the manufacturers instructions. Automatic dispensers and liquid injectors, if any, shall be properly installed and maintained.

findings.title: Hand washing sinks installed, located, accessible
findings.comment:
Observed hand sink containing food debris and plastic object.
Hand washing stations should be used only for hand washing.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
Observed dirty floor
Floor needs to be in good repair.
750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

findings.title: Lighting provided as required.  Fixtures shielded
findings.comment:
Observed poor lighting in walk-in cooler
Adequate lighting needs to be present in all areas.
750-1230(a) Permanently fixed artificial light sources shall be installed to provide at least 20 foot-candles of light on all food preparation surfaces and and at equipment or utensil washing areas.

findings.title: Rooms clean, lockers provided and used, clean
findings.comment:
Observed personal items in food storage area.
Personal items should be placed in designated area away from food.
750-1280 Adequate area must be provided for the storage of employee belongings segregated from the food preparation and food storage area to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all employee belongings.
